newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end higher on Q1 GDP, rates hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end higher on Q1 GDP, rates hopes.

text.p: Mexican stocks pushed further ahead at the close of trade on Monday, driven by favorable GDP data and a forecast decline in domestic interest rates, traders said.
"I feel the market reacted at the close to a forecast decline of at least 30 basis points, which combined with GDP, tells you the economy is on track," a desk trader said.

The leading IPC share index .MXX ended up 31.02 points, or 0.80 percent, to 3,921.38. The Finance Ministry announced that Mexico's GDP grew 5.1 percent during the first quarter of 1997 compared with a year ago.

Fixed-income analysts said rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes could fall up to 50 basis points from 18.91 percent at the central bank primary auction of government securities on Tuesday evening. Analysts said dealing was cautious ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rate policy.

"The market was very cautious because of tomorrow. Opinions differ and there is more uncertainty this time. Most decided not to raise the stakes," said Gerardo Copca, associate research director at the Arka brokerage in Mexico City.
Trading volume .TV.MX totalled 83.7 million shares, but traders pointed out that cross trades accounted for more than 30 million shares.
"The Dow also encouraged the market, if it is gaining, it could be moving ahead of good news on rates," Copca added.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended up 34.21 points at 7,228.88.
"There was real buying," another desk trader said. "If (U.S.) rates do go up, risks are high if you go long or short, so most dealers squared positions."
Dealers said Telmex and Bancomer weighed most on the upside, as they together accounted for one-fifth of all shares traded, not including one hefty cross trade.

Telecomms firm Telmex gained six centavos to 17.18 pesos, shadowing its ADRs, which ended up 1/8 at 43-1/2 while financial group Bancomer gained five centavos to 2.99 pesos on hopes that lower interest rates would ease its past-due loans burden, traders said.
Traders also drew attention to gains by cement maker Cemex, which rose 1.10 pesos to 29.50 pesos.
"Cemex responded to the announced diversification in its business and inroads it is making in the Asian market. They have really turned the tables on their positioning," a desk trader said.
On the broad market, a total of 111 stocks changed hands, of which gains outnumbered declines by 48 to 38.
